$comment: DRIFT THE SHADOW ALREADY FOUND, so it stops taking the repo down while the
operator decides what to do about it.
The shadow run compares each secret's GitHub value against its Bitwarden value
and fails the job when they disagree. That is the right default and it worked:
it caught three secrets whose two copies hold DIFFERENT VALUES. But the compare
step runs near the TOP of every job, so each finding also stopped that job's real
work -- and the three names below sit in the most load-bearing jobs in the repo:
the CI watchdog, the Claude review gate, autopilot, both CD deploys, the preview
deploy, the Stripe sandbox job and the account E2E battery.
On 2026-09-03 that cost the watchdog entirely: run 33704079162 reported failure
having monitored NOTHING, because the compare exited 1 before the monitor step
ran. A temporary migration scaffold had switched off the mechanism that guards
every other CI run, and the only symptom was a red watchdog -- which reads like
the watchdog working.
An entry here means: this drift is KNOWN, RECORDED, and belongs to the operator.
It does NOT weaken the shadow. Any name not listed here still fails its job on
mismatch, an EMPTY value on either side is still fatal for listed names too (an
empty is a broken fetch, not a known drift), and a listed name that starts
MATCHING fails the job until its entry is deleted -- an exemption cannot outlive
the condition that justified it.
This file is deleted with the org secrets, along with the rest of the shadow.
Only the operator can resolve these: GitHub secrets are write-only, so no session
can read the GitHub value to reconcile it with Bitwarden.

STRIPE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET.reason: BLOCKER: the two sides hold different VALUES, and the reason is now known: this is a stripe listen CLI secret, not an endpoint secret. .ci/lib/account.sh:391 and private/account/e2e/run-stripe-e2e.sh:120 both obtain it by scraping `stripe listen` output, and account.sh:235 documents it as auto-captured -- every listen session mints a fresh whsec_ that expires in 24h, so neither stored copy is authoritative and the compare can never pass while the value is stored at all. It CANNOT simply be deleted: cd-deploy-worker.yml:277-279 makes it the edge/preview www worker's STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and .ci/scripts/deploy/set-www-worker-secrets.sh:89 requires it non-empty, so deleting it fails every edge deploy. The E2E path no longer reads it (run-account-e2e.sh now uses the STRIPE_E2E_WEBHOOK_SECRET fixture); the edge deploy is the sole remaining consumer and it needs a real endpoint signing secret before this entry can go.
STRIPE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET.found_in_run: 33691632299 (CANCELLED -- its logs no longer return any shadow verdict line; the finding stands on the code path above, not on that run)

RELEASE_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY.reason: BLOCKER: the two copies are the SAME KEY stored as different bytes. Proven 2026-09-04 without reading the GitHub value: the Bitwarden copy (uuid b6c8d767-...-b4b900b82d3a, fetched with the pinned sm-action) carries primary fingerprint 42EAD1408A684AB8F185F03F49BA687F0527C72B and subkey A9B4F1271093AC04C9DF310C29D8083F0A34F01D, identical to .ci/keys/gpg-public.asc; and https://releases.rediacc.com/apt/edge/dists/stable/Release.gpg (signed 2026-09-02 by CD with the GITHUB copy, org secret GPG_PRIVATE_KEY mapped in ci.yml:947-975) gives 'Good signature' with that committed public key, using that subkey. RELEASE_GPG_PASSPHRASE matches. So signing works from either copy and the drift is byte-level -- an armored block stored with or without its trailing newline is the likely shape; the compare now prints which kind it saw ([whitespace-only ...] or [content differs]) without exposing a byte. GitHub secrets are write-only, so which side to normalise cannot be decided from here; the babysit did not overwrite an unreadable org secret on its own authority.
RELEASE_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY.found_in_run: 33904687989 (Stage Artifacts, job 101132642274: 'shadow RELEASE_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY MISMATCH', the four other names in the job match)

$resolution: WHAT THE OPERATOR ACTUALLY HAS TO DO, so this is not rediscovered.
There is no command that reads a GitHub secret. They are write-only: `gh` can list
names and never contents. So no session can compare the two copies; the comparison in
CI is the ONLY place both values exist at once, and it sees them as hashes.
For each name below, decide which copy is authoritative and overwrite the other, then
DELETE its entry here -- the gate makes that non-optional, because an excused name that
starts MATCHING fails its job until the entry goes.
RESOLVED 2026-09-03, both by writing Bitwarden's value over the GitHub copy:
ANTHROPIC_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN -- and the cause was NOT what this file guessed.
It supposed a rotation applied under one name had not reached the other. The real
cause was a THIRD copy: a REPO-level CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN shadowed the org-level
one, so `secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` resolved to the repo copy in every
workflow, and that is what the shadow compared. Overwriting the org secret alone
would have changed nothing observable. Fix applied: set the org copy from Bitwarden
(visibility `selected`, account/console/renet preserved), THEN delete the repo copy,
in that order so a verified value resolves at every moment. rediacc/console now has
exactly two repo-level secrets, BREAKPOINT_TUNNEL_TOKEN and BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN.
ACCOUNT_SERVER_API_KEY -- an admin key with no customers; the operator's ruling was
consistency and central management, so Bitwarden won. Set from Bitwarden, visibility
`selected` on rediacc/console preserved.
STILL OPEN: STRIPE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and it is a different SHAPE of problem --
not a drift to resolve by picking a side. See its reason above: it is a `stripe listen`
CLI secret that expires 24h after minting, so neither stored copy is authoritative and
no overwrite can make the compare pass while the value is stored at all. It cannot
simply be deleted either, because cd-deploy-worker.yml:277-279 makes it the edge and
preview www worker's STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and set-www-worker-secrets.sh:89 requires it
non-empty. What that implies is worth stating: edge has been deployed with a webhook
secret that died 24h after it was captured, so its sandbox webhook path cannot verify
anything -- invisible only because all four sandbox destinations are Disabled.
The resolution is to mint a real endpoint signing secret for the edge-eu sandbox
destination and store THAT; the published E2E fixture must not be used, because edge is
internet-reachable and a known secret would let anyone forge sandbox webhooks against it.
